prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose How You Want to Begin", "Select a quick pre-built companion or build your custom desktop pet."]
1: ["Signing in links your pet securely. Existing pets will be automatically restored to your desktop."]
2: ["Review Your Pet Companion", "Check your selected traits before bringing your pet to life on your desktop.", "Confirm & Generate"]
3: ["Sign In & Keep My Pet"]
4: ["Upload Pet Photos for Custom Rendering", "Provide clear photos of your pet from multiple angles for best accuracy."]
5: ["Preparing Your Pet Desktop Workspace", "Your pet is being initialized. It will appear on your screen shortly."]
6: ["Meet Your New Desktop Companion", "Click your pet to interact, drag to move across windows, or access pet settings from your system tray.", "Start Playing"]
7: ["Is Your Pet Visible on Desktop?", "Look around your screen! If your pet is hiding or off-screen, click below to center it.", "Pet Is Ready!"]
8: []
9: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets", "Adopt a ready-to-play pet instantly or create a custom pet from your own photos in just a few steps.", "Explore Paths"]
